newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lion, Telecom lead NZ shares toward peaks by close.
newsitem.headline: Lion, Telecom lead NZ shares toward peaks by close.

text.p: * NZ shares close near record levels as money jitters pass
* Telecom continues to drive index, helped by Lion Nathan
* Overseas interest remains strong in selected bluechips
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +18.31 at 2,510.61
378 +2 * NZSC cap index -0.35 at 5,238.97
345 +3 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +6.87 at 1,990.62
392 +6 * Volume NZ$64 million. Futures untraded
765 +7 * Other movers - +9 +10
Telecom gained seven cents to close at NZ$7.65, while Lion's six cent gain took it to $3.92 and together they helped the NZSE Top40 index gain 18.31 points to close at 2,510.61.

Luke Koekoek at JB Were in Auckland said the overseas investors who had made their presence felt late in the day, especially in Telecom, were taking comfort from a calmer dollar and lower 90-day rates following their recent ructions.

"Obviously we did have a big correction quickly, and the dollar consolidating at current levels is definitely comforting for those guys, (so) you might see a little bit more offshore money come into this market," he said.
Brokers observed that Brierley Investments was one of the few blue chips to look uncomfortable, as its price has slipped off a high three weeks ago and shown no sign of rebound.
Brierley has suffered from its exposure to the competitive UK hotel market through its Thistle associate.
Sources said during the day Brierley had sold a stake in Fletcher Energy recently but it remains unconfirmed.
Air New Zealand, Fletcher Energy and forestry sector stocks Fletcher Paper and Carter Holt Harvey are seen taking a boost from the lower dollar.
Koekoek noted that Fletcher Paper had managed to add another three cents, to $3.45, today despite an ongoing Canadian strike.
